items.t: Ibovespa Gains 0.54% to 169,405.74 Points in Mid-Session Trade
sum: The Ibovespa advanced in Monday's session as investors responded to renewed assurances on Brazil's fiscal direction. At 13:50 Brasília time, the benchmark stood at 169,405.74 points, according to The Rio Times. That represented a gain of 907.29 points, or 0.54%, from Friday's closing level of 168,498.45 points.

The advance followed a national address by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on Sunday in which he reaffirmed his commitment to fiscal responsibility and said the government would work to create conditions for lower interest rates. As reported by Trading Economics, the statement helped lift the index toward the 170,000-point area, although the government did not provide detailed spending-adjustment measures.

The backdrop remains demanding for Brazilian assets. The Selic rate was held at 13.75% on November 4, while investors are monitoring inflation and interest-rate expectations. The Rio Times reported that the central bank's Focus survey was due on Monday and that minutes from the Copom meeting were scheduled for Tuesday. Those releases may provide further clues about the future path of monetary policy.

Market performance was mixed across major sectors. The Rio Times' intraday board showed industrial stocks leading with an average gain of 2.78%, while mining shares rose 2.57%. WEG gained 3.98%, Gerdau preferred shares advanced 3.11%, and Vale rose 2.55%. Financials also contributed, with Itaú Unibanco up 1.38% and Bradesco preferred shares 1.83% higher.

Energy stocks moved in the opposite direction. Petrobras preferred shares were down 0.26%, while PRIO fell 2.08%. Trading Economics attributed the pressure on Petrobras to weaker international oil prices as hopes for US-Iran diplomacy reduced the oil-market risk premium. The Rio Times board showed Brent crude down 4.23% at the time of its intraday reading.

Monday's advance extended the rebound from Friday's 1.39% gain, but the index was still testing the 170,000-point area identified by The Rio Times as near-term resistance. The session therefore showed improved sentiment without, by itself, confirming a lasting change in trend. Investors continued to balance fiscal promises against the need for concrete measures, elevated interest rates and a weaker Brazilian real.

Australia increased coking coal exports by 1.8% y/y in October
sum: In October 2026, coking coal exports from Australia decreased by 10.8% compared to September, to 12.49 million tonnes, interrupting the recovery seen in August and September. This was reported by BigMint.
Despite the monthly decline, shipment volumes were 1.8% higher than in October 2025. Overall, exports for the ten months of 2026 increased by 4.3% to 126.52 million tonnes.
The overall growth masks a significant shift in supply destinations: a sharp increase in purchases by China offset the decline in exports to India and South Korea.

Analysts note that about 1.90 million tonnes (15.2%) of October exports currently have no identified destination, leaving room for further adjustment of statistics for individual importing countries. However, the main trend of the year remains unchanged: China is taking an increasing share of Australian coking coal, intensifying competition for other buyers.

As GMK Center reported earlier, the shortage of coking coal in China will continue until 2027, ensuring high demand for imports despite the authorities’ attempts to restore domestic production and stabilize prices. The supply shock caused by the mine accident in Shanxi province in May will have long-lasting consequences. According to Bloomberg Intelligence (BI) analysts, the recovery of production will be gradual due to strict safety measures. Increased supplies from Mongolia, Australia and Russia will partially offset the shortage, but will not be able to close the gap completely.

4 Steel Producer Stocks in Focus as Industry Gains on Higher Prices
sum: The Zacks Steel Producers industry is poised to benefit from an uptick in steel prices. A resilient non-residential construction market and recovering demand in the automotive space also act as tailwinds for the industry.

Higher U.S. steel prices have created a favorable landscape for American steel producers. Tightened supply and higher end-market demand are driving steel prices. Players from the industry, such as Nucor Corporation NUE, Ternium S.A. TX, Gerdau S.A. GGB and L.B. Foster Company FSTR are set to benefit from these trends.

The Zacks Steel Producers industry serves a vast spectrum of end-use industries, such as automotive, construction, appliance, container, packaging, industrial machinery, mining equipment, transportation, and oil and gas, with various steel products. These products include hot-rolled and cold-rolled coils and sheets, hot-dipped and galvanized coils and sheets, reinforcing bars, billets and blooms, wire rods, strip mill plates, standard and line pipe, and mechanical tubing products. Steel is primarily produced using two methods — Blast Furnace and Electric Arc Furnace. It is regarded as the backbone of the manufacturing industry. The automotive and construction markets have historically been the largest consumers of steel. The housing and construction sector accounts for roughly half of the world's total steel consumption.

Elevated Steel Prices Bode Well: U.S. steel prices recovered in the fourth quarter of 2025, following the lows seen in the third quarter, and the momentum continued in the first quarter of 2026. Overall demand weakness and abundant steel mill output dragged benchmark hot-rolled coil ("HRC") prices below $800 per short ton in late August and continuing through early September. HRC prices rebounded in the fourth quarter on major steel mills' price increase, extending lead times and tightening supply, partly due to plant outages and reduced imports driven by tariffs. The recovery, which has been more pronounced since November, has led to HRC prices surging to above $1,100 per short ton. Global steel prices have also increased due to supply constraints driven by China's steel output reductions, as well as price hikes by steel mills amid higher raw material, energy and freight costs triggered by the Middle East Conflict.

Turkey’s Koç Group has become one of Stegra’s new shareholders
sum: According to the financial publication Dagens Industri, Swedish green steel startup Stegra has issued a total of 850 million new shares to finance the construction of its plant.
This issue increased the total number of the company’s shares by 23%, and among the new shareholders is Koç Group, Turkey’s largest industrial conglomerate.

As the publication notes, in November 2025, Stegra announced that an additional SEK 10 billion was needed to complete the construction of the steel plant in Boden. However, according to Dagens Industri sources, as a result of subsequent negotiations with financiers, the amount more than doubled.

As a reminder, in November last year, Stegra, which was seeking additional funding for its project, received a state grant from Sweden in the amount of SEK 390 million ($40.9 million, approximately €37 million). The support was provided on the condition that the company secure funds to complete the project by spring 2026.

Stegra is building a large-scale plant for the production of environmentally friendly steel in Boden. It will consist of an electrolyzer, a direct reduction plant, two electric arc furnaces, as well as cold rolling and finishing shops. Production is expected to start in the second half of 2026, with the plant reaching full capacity in 2028.
